text.p: Delta Air Lines Inc's board of directors declined to renew former Chairman Ronald Allen's contract, partly out of concern that his cost cuts were eating into employee morale and customer service, the Wall Street Journal reported Friday.
Though the cuts initiated under Allen helped pull the nation's third-largest carrier out of a financial tailspin, company directors were not pleased with his management style, the Journal said.
One unnamed source told the newspper that company directors began weighing "an accumulation of abrasions over time" that undermined confidence in Allen's leadership.
Earlier this month, the company announced that Allen decided to retire when his contract expired July 31.
Allen declined to comment to the Journal about his departure. "I just cannot comment beyond the... press release" announcing his retirement, Allen said in a handwritten note.
